reason:
The plan itself is safe and sensible. It comes to 41 miles after a 40-mile week (53 the week before), keeps Marisol's five days with Monday and Friday off, has one marathon-pace session on Wednesday and a 16-mile easy long run on Sunday. Every day can be run as written, with heart-rate caps. Nothing here is a sharp jump.

The big failure is that it never answers Marisol's question. She asked whether she should double to 80 miles next week with twice-a-day runs to catch up to her club mate. A coach has to say a clear no to that: it is a risky jump that invites injury. She needs to hear why, and that 70-mile weeks are built over years. The draft only hints at this with "maintain volume," so she could still go ahead with her plan. Answering the athlete is one of the things that weighs most, and the question was a risky one.

Other problems:
- It says she had "no runs missed or overruns," which the card doesn't support.
- It doesn't mention the heavy legs early in the week.
- It doesn't tie the plan to her 3:45 goal or a timeline.

The schedule is fine, but the reply misses what mattered most this week.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Maintain volume with a single quality session and a slightly longer long run to keep building toward the marathon goal.
You did the prescribed week as planned, no runs missed or overruns. The build phase wants steady volume with one quality session and rest on Monday and Friday.
Next week:
Mon: rest
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate <150, flat route. Loosens legs after rest.
Wed: quality, 9 mi, 6 at marathon pace, 3 easy, heart rate 150–160 BPM. Builds tempo.
Thu: easy, 6 mi, heart rate <150. Recovers from quality.
Fri: rest
Sat: easy, 4 mi, relaxed, low effort.
Sun: long, 16 mi easy, heart rate <150. Stretches endurance.
